_strings.@@08d0a50b8ec9: Qualified Caregiving Expense Credit (Credit Code 204) — Taxpayers who pay qualified caregiving expenses for a qualifying family member who is at least age 62 OR has been determined disabled by the Social Security Administration. A qualifying family member includes the taxpayer or someone related to the taxpayer by blood, marriage, or adoption. Qualified services (home health agency, personal care, homemaker, adult day care, respite care, medically necessary equipment) must be obtained from an organization or individual NOT related to the taxpayer or family member. Expenses already subtracted/excluded from Georgia net taxable income do not qualify.
_strings.@@151b7062a01e: Low Income Tax Credit (Credit Code 211) — Georgia residents whose Federal adjusted gross income (FAGI) is less than $20,000 and who are not claimed (or eligible to be claimed) as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal or Georgia return. Cannot be claimed by an inmate in a correctional facility. Part-year residents qualify only if they were Georgia residents at the end of the tax year. Credit is computed per exemption (self, spouse, and natural/legally adopted children; for this credit dependents do NOT include unborn dependents).
_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@2be0e3aab5c6: Child and Dependent Care Expense Credit (Credit Code 202) — Georgia taxpayers who claimed and were allowed the federal child & dependent care expense credit under Internal Revenue Code Section 21 on their federal Form 1040. The Georgia credit is a flat percentage of that allowed federal credit; the booklet does not impose a separate Georgia income limit (federal Section 21 eligibility rules govern).
_strings.@@2f53759c8a68: Georgia Dept. of Revenue, PO Box 740392, Atlanta, GA 30374-0392 (for Form 500 and 500 EZ returns expecting a refund or with no balance due)
_strings.@@3545035d9967: GA Form 500 (Rev. 08/30/23) 2023 blank return - Line 8 'Federal adjusted gross income (From Federal Form 1040)', Line 9 Schedule 1 adjustments, Line 4 residency status (1 full-year/2 part-year/3 nonresident), 'use Form 500 Schedule 3 if you are a part-year or nonresident filer'
_strings.@@44a3d7314703: Disabled Person Home Purchase or Retrofit Credit (Credit Code 201) — A permanently disabled person (the taxpayer or the taxpayer's spouse on a joint return) who has been issued a permanent parking permit (or special permanent parking permit) by the Department of Revenue, and who purchases a new single-family home containing all four required accessibility features, or retrofits an existing single-family home with one or more of those features (no-step entrance; 32-inch interior passage doorways; bathroom-wall reinforcements for grab bars; accessible light switches/outlets).
_strings.@@4cf945d1e9e4: Credit amounts/limits are not independently verified: State credits were researched from the cited DOR sources and are not tax advice — confirm each amount and your eligibility at the cited source before claiming it.
_strings.@@4d42ad525021: Mailing address: Some state facts could not be independently re-confirmed — see the pack's `unverified` list; confirm at the cited DOR source before relying on a specific figure/address.
_strings.@@52334a4d85d3: Treaty conformity — GA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from GA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the GA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Georgia conforms. The resident return (Form 500) starts from federal adjusted gross income (Form 500, Line 8: "Federal adjusted gross income (From Federal Form 1040)"), and the GA DOR confirms "Georgia Individual Income tax is based on the taxpayer's federal adjusted gross income, adjustments that are required by Georgia law." Adjustments are made only on Form 500 Schedule 1. Schedule 1 ADDITIONS (lines 1-5) are limited to: (1) Interest on Non-Georgia Municipal and State Bonds, (2) Lump Sum Distributions, (3) Depreciation, (4) Net operating loss carryover deducted on the Federal return, and (5) Other (Specify) -- there is NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA add-back). To the contrary, the IT-511 booklet expressly lists as a SUBTRACTION item 10: "Income from any fund, program or system which is specifically exempted by Federal law or treaty." Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and GA neither adds it back nor otherwise re-taxes it (and explicitly recognizes the treaty exemption), it flows through untaxed.
_strings.@@ba474fd11008: Form 500 (Georgia Individual Income Tax Return), Rev. 08/30/23 for tax year 2023; short-form Form 500-EZ also available for eligible full-year residents.
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.
_strings.@@eeeb5bf1a56a: Form 500 with Schedule 3 (part-year residents and nonresidents file the same Form 500 and complete Form 500 Schedule 3 to calculate Georgia taxable income). There is no separate nonresident return number; the residency status box on Form 500 Line 4 (1=full-year resident, 2=part-year resident, 3=nonresident) designates status.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 500, Line 16 "Tax (Use Tax Rate Schedule in the IT-511 Tax Booklet)"; IT-511 p.12: "Line 16: Take the amount from Line 15c and use the Tax Rate Schedule starting on page 59 to determine your tax liability." Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,300 — Additional standard deduction per '65 or over' checkbox, Form 500 Line 11b (self and spouse each; standard-deduction filers only). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on Form 500 Line 11b.); blind ($1,300 — Additional standard deduction per 'Blind' checkbox, Form 500 Line 11b (self and spouse each; standard-deduction filers only). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on Form 500 Line 11b.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form 500, Line 10 "Georgia adjusted gross income" (Line 8 federal AGI from Form 1040, net of Line 9 adjustments from Form 500 Schedule 1) for a FULL-YEAR resident. The op then subtracts the shipped per-status figure (which is Georgia's standard deduction PLUS the per-status personal exemption — see notes) and $3,000 per dependent to reach Line 15c Georgia taxable income, then applies the Tax Rate Schedule. Pass exemptions_count=0 (no 'personal' key is shipped; the personal exemption is already inside the per-status standard_deduction figure) and dependents_count = Form 500 Line 7c (qualified dependents plus unborn dependents). Do not use this op if you itemize deductions, claim a Georgia NOL (Line 15b), or file as a part-year resident/nonresident (Schedule 3 prorates deductions and exemptions) — compute those on the form. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — Form 500 Line 8 is federal AGI and Line 10 Georgia AGI = federal AGI +/- Schedule 1 adjustments; supply Line 10 as taxable_base (the op subtracts the combined standard-deduction+personal-exemption figure and per-dependent $3,000). Form 500 line roles cross-checked against the repo GA formpack (11a standard deduction; 14a/14b exemptions; 14c=14a+14b). COMPOSITION OF THE SHIPPED standard_deduction: it is Georgia's printed standard deduction (Form 500 Line 11a: $5,400 Single/HoH/QSS, $7,100 MFJ, $3,550 MFS) PLUS the per-status personal exemption (Form 500 Line 14a: $2,700 x 1 for status A Single and status D HoH/QSS; $3,700 x 2 = $7,400 for status B MFJ; $3,700 x 1 for status C MFS). Georgia's per-exemption amount varies by filing status ($2,700 vs $3,700), which the engine's single 'personal' scalar cannot express, so it is folded into the per-status figure. The combined totals $8,100 / $14,500 / $7,250 are printed as such in the booklet's own 'standard deduction and personal exemptions' filing-requirement chart (IT-511 p.9). Pass exemptions_count=0 — no 'personal' exemption key is shipped, so exemptions_count is ignored. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE: Georgia files QSS under filing status D 'Head of Household or Qualifying Surviving Spouse' — pass head_of_household to this op, NOT married_filing_jointly. The bracket schedule is identical to MFJ, but the QSS/HoH deduction+exemption total is $8,100, not MFJ's $14,500; mapping QSS to MFJ would understate tax. One printed bracket schedule covers 'Married Filing Joint or Head of Household' (IT-511 p.59) — the head_of_household brackets here duplicate married_filing_jointly per that schedule; Single and Married Filing Separate have their own printed schedules. ITEMIZERS NOT MODELED: the shipped figures assume the Georgia standard deduction. If you itemized on your federal return (or are MFS and your spouse itemizes), you MUST itemize on the Georgia return (Line 12c = federal Schedule A total less Georgia adjustments); if you used the federal standard deduction you must use the Georgia standard deduction. Itemizers must compute Lines 12-16 on the form. Additional standard deduction of $1,300 per checkbox (age 65 or over and/or blind, self and spouse each — up to 4 checkboxes, Form 500 Line 11b) is NOT applied by calc.state_tax; standard-deduction filers only. Enter on Line 11b. Georgia NOL not modeled: Form 500 Line 15b (Georgia NOL utilized, limited to 80% of Line 15a income for losses from tax years 2018+) is subtracted before Line 15c taxable income. Part-year residents and nonresidents not modeled: they skip Form 500 Lines 9-14 and use Schedule 3, which prorates the standard deduction, additional deduction, and exemptions by the Georgia-income ratio (Schedule 3 Line 9). This pack's subtractions apply only to full-year residents. Taxpayers required to file federal Form 1040NR generally may NOT take the Georgia standard deduction (IT-511 p.10: most are allowed only the personal exemption and limited Form 1040NR Schedule A itemized deductions). Printed 'Amount of Tax Is' constants, Single schedule (IT-511 p.59): $8.00 / $38.00 / $83.00 / $143.00 versus exact cumulative bracket sums $7.50 / $37.50 / $82.50 / $142.50 — each rounded up by $0.50; the top constant $230.00 equals the exact sum. Worksheet math using the printed constants can therefore differ from pure marginal bracket math by up to $0.50 (at most $1 after rounding) for Single taxable income between $750 and $7,000. The MFJ/HoH constants ($10/$50/$110/$190/$340) and MFS constants ($5/$25/$55/$95/$170) equal the exact cumulative sums. Optional tax table, no mandate: IT-511 pp.63-65 print a Georgia Income Tax Table in $100 bands for taxable income under $100,000, but its use is optional — 'A taxpayer can use the tax tables starting on page 63 or the Georgia Tax Rate Schedule' (p.59), and the table's own footnote states: 'The tax table is not exact and may cause the amounts on the return to be changed. It is recommended to use the tax rate schedule for the exact amount of tax.' Table values (computed at band midpoints) may differ from bracket math by a few dollars within a band. CREDITS (subtracted from tax, NOT modeled and NOT base reductions): Low Income Credit (Form 500 Line 17 — a per-exemption CREDIT of $5-$26 for federal AGI under $20,000, not an exemption); Other State(s) Tax Credit (Line 18); IND-CR series 200 credits (Line 19); Schedule 2 series 100 credits (Line 20). Total credits (Line 21) cannot exceed Line 16 tax. 2023 is Georgia's final graduated-rate year; no mid-2023 retroactive rate change applies to tax year 2023. Per the 2023 IT-511 'What's New' (p.7): 'Effective January 1, 2024, the income tax rate will be 5.39%. Additionally, personal exemptions have been repealed except for the $4,000 dependent exemption. Finally, Georgia standard deductions have increased to $24,000 for Married Filing Joint returns and $12,000 for Single, Head of Household, and Married Filing Separate returns.' Do not use this 2023 pack for 2024+. Rounding: the booklet's worked examples state amounts are 'rounded to the nearest dollar' (IT-511 p.60); this pack rounds half-up to whole dollars, which reproduces both booklet examples exactly ($5,125 Single -> $138; $77,878 MFJ -> $4,243).
